blocks.prompt: 21 Solve the following trigonometric equation: \(\frac{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x}{\sin x + \cos x} - \frac{\sin x}{\sqrt{1 + \tan^2 x}} = \frac{1}{2}\)
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do fractions hain. Pehli mein cubes ka jama hai jo factorise ho kar chhota ho jata hai. Doosri mein \(\sqrt{1 + \tan^2 x}\) chhupa hua \(\sqrt{\sec^2 x}\) hai, aur yahin asal imtihan hai.
Find kya karna hai? \([0, 2\pi]\) mein solutions aur general solution.
Rule: \(a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)\), \(1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x\), aur \(\sqrt{p^2} = |p|\) (absolute value, yani hamesha positive).
Plan: absolute value ki wajah se do cases banenge: \(\cos x > 0\) aur \(\cos x < 0\). Har case alag hal karenge aur sirf woh jawab rakhenge jo apne case ki shart poori karte hon.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x}{\sin x + \cos x} - \frac{\sin x}{\sqrt{1 + \tan^2 x}} = \frac{1}{2}\).
Maloom karna: \([0, 2\pi]\) mein solutions aur general solution.
Tareeqa: cubes ka formula, \(1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x\), aur \(\sqrt{p^2} = |p|\). Pabandi: \(\sin x + \cos x \neq 0\) (denominator) aur \(\cos x \neq 0\) (warna \(\tan x\) defined nahi).

Pehli term
\[\dfrac{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x}{\sin x + \cos x}\]
\[= \sin^2 x - \sin x\cos x + \cos^2 x\]
\[= 1 - \sin x\cos x\]
Kyun: \(a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)\) se numerator mein \((\sin x + \cos x)\) factor nikla jo denominator se cancel ho gaya (pabandi ke mutabiq woh zero nahi). Phir \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\).
Yahan \(a = \sin x\) aur \(b = \cos x\) hain; formula ka beech wala hissa \(a^2 - ab + b^2\) hai, jis mein \(ab\) ke saath minus hota hai.

Doosri term
\[\sqrt{1 + \tan^2 x} = \sqrt{\sec^2 x} = |\sec x|\]
Kyun: square root ka jawab kabhi negative nahi hota. Is liye \(\sqrt{\sec^2 x}\) sirf tab \(\sec x\) hai jab \(\sec x\) positive ho, yani \(\cos x > 0\). Agar \(\cos x\) negative ho to \(\sqrt{\sec^2 x} = -\sec x\) hoga. Misaal: \(\sqrt{(-2)^2} = \sqrt{4} = 2\), \(-2\) nahi.
Dhyan dein: yahan seedha \(\sec x\) likh dena is sawal ki sab se bari aur aam ghalti hai.

Case (a): \(\cos x > 0\) (quadrant I ya IV)
\[\dfrac{\sin x}{\sec x} = \sin x\cos x\]
\[1 - \sin x\cos x - \sin x\cos x = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[1 - 2\sin x\cos x = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\sin 2x = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: is case mein \(|\sec x| = \sec x\), aur \(\sec x\) se divide karna \(\cos x\) se multiply karne ke barabar hai. Do \(\sin x\cos x\) mil kar \(2\sin x\cos x = \sin 2x\) bane, phir \(1 - \sin 2x = \frac{1}{2}\) se \(\sin 2x = \frac{1}{2}\).
Is case mein \(x\) pehle ya chauthe quadrant mein hai; yeh shart aage jawab chhantne (filter karne) mein kaam aayegi.

\(\sin 2x = \frac{1}{2}\) hal karein
\[2x = \tfrac{\pi}{6} + 2n\pi \text{ ya } \tfrac{5\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\]
\[x = \tfrac{\pi}{12} + n\pi \text{ ya } \tfrac{5\pi}{12} + n\pi\]
\([0, 2\pi]\) mein: \(\frac{\pi}{12}, \frac{5\pi}{12}, \frac{13\pi}{12}, \frac{17\pi}{12}\).
Kyun: sine positive hai to angle \(2x\) pehle ya doosre quadrant mein, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{6}\). Phir 2 se divide kiya, to period \(2\pi\) bhi \(\pi\) ban gaya.

Sirf \(\cos x > 0\) wali values rakhein
\[\tfrac{\pi}{12}, \tfrac{5\pi}{12} \text{ (quadrant I): qabool}\]
\[\tfrac{13\pi}{12}, \tfrac{17\pi}{12} \text{ (quadrant III): rad}\]
Kyun: Case (a) ki buniyad hi yeh shart thi ke \(\cos x > 0\). \(\frac{13\pi}{12}\) aur \(\frac{17\pi}{12}\) teesre quadrant mein hain jahan cosine negative hota hai, is liye yeh is case ke jawab ho hi nahi sakte.

Case (b): \(\cos x < 0\) (quadrant II ya III)
\[\dfrac{\sin x}{|\sec x|} = -\sin x\cos x\]
\[1 - \sin x\cos x + \sin x\cos x = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[1 = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
Yeh namumkin hai, is liye \(\cos x < 0\) par koi solution nahi.
Kyun: yahan \(|\sec x| = -\sec x\), to doosri term ka sign ulta ho gaya aur dono \(\sin x\cos x\) cancel ho gaye. Left side har jagah 1 reh gayi, jo kabhi \(\frac{1}{2}\) nahi ban sakti.
Yani doosre aur teesre quadrant mein equation ka koi jawab hai hi nahi; yeh baat graph mein us seedhi line se bhi nazar aati hai jo 1 ki unchai par chalti hai.

General solution
\[\left\{\tfrac{\pi}{12} + 2n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\tfrac{5\pi}{12} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
Kyun: qabool shuda values sirf \(2\pi\) ke baad dohraati hain, kyunke \(\cos x\) ka sign \(2\pi\) ke baad wapas aata hai, \(\pi\) ke baad nahi. Dono values par \(\cos x \neq 0\) aur \(\sin x + \cos x > 0\), is liye equation wahan defined hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{\pi}{12} + n\pi\) likhne se rejected values \(\frac{13\pi}{12}\) aur \(\frac{17\pi}{12}\) wapas aa jati hain.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \tfrac{\pi}{12}:\ \sin x\cos x = \tfrac{1}{2}\sin\tfrac{\pi}{6} = \tfrac{1}{4}\]
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \left(1 - \tfrac{1}{4}\right) - \tfrac{1}{4} = \tfrac{1}{2} \;\checkmark\]
\[x = \tfrac{13\pi}{12}:\ \text{L.H.S.} = \tfrac{3}{4} + \tfrac{1}{4} = 1 \neq \tfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{13\pi}{12}\) par bhi \(\sin x\cos x = \frac{1}{4}\) hai, magar wahan \(\cos x < 0\) hai, is liye doosri term \(-\frac{1}{4}\) ban kar plus ho jati hai aur jawab 1 aata hai. Isi se saabit hota hai ke us value ko rad karna sahi tha.
Graph bhi yehi kehta hai: jahan \(\cos x < 0\) hai wahan left side ki line 1 par seedhi rehti hai aur \(\frac{1}{2}\) wali line ko kabhi nahi chhooti.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of the left side of the equation for x from 0 to 2 pi together with the horizontal line y equals one half. The left side equals 1 minus sine 2x where cosine x is positive and equals 1 where cosine x is negative; it meets the line only at x equals pi over 12 and 5 pi over 12.
answer_figure.caption: Left side sirf x = π/12 aur 5π/12 par y = 1/2 se milti hai; jahan cos x < 0 hai wahan yeh 1 par hi rehti hai (original drawing)
